transitModes.Public identity: Road service, wilderness freight, slow public movement, and weather-flexible routes. Caravans are still necessary because not every settlement trusts engines.
Harbor, river, lake, canal, reef, and island service. Ferry captains are tide readers first and pilots second.
Longer water routes using marine logic improved by ichor heat, compact engines, and cleaner power cycles.
Pressure-safe underwater passenger and freight craft; amphibious access keeps them classified as submarine routes even when land locks are involved.
Steam-electric ichor hybrid rail with stations, signals, grades, braking, and public timetables.
Airborne galleons and high-altitude service using lift lattices, sail-field coupling, and vector nozzles.
Capital-threshold service through passes, locks, batch limits, cooldowns, and receiving-hall clearance.
